capture_audit.interpretation: The bound 384-row serialization contains one repeated hidden state and proposal ID zero. Request/depth recall is therefore 384 replications of one decision and cannot establish workload-level retrieval quality.

decision.next_action: Close this admission without GPU work. A successor may recapture genuinely distinct verifier hidden states, hash-bind them, and rerun this same offline W8A8/coordinate retrieval consumer before any H200 claim.
decision.reason: weight_variance_bf16_coordinates_256 recovers the bound reference at 8192/262144 candidates with an analytical materialized-score bound of 1.023 ms, but the 384-row capture contains one unique hidden state. That is insufficient to spend a GPU claim or claim request/depth robustness.

full_head_reference_top1_identity.softcap_note: The stock fused softcap is monotone, so pre-softcap dot-product argmax is identical.

h200_geometry_and_first_consumer_path.falsifier: A target-H200 component must hash-bind the same weight and a genuinely diverse capture, preserve every full-head top-1, and beat 24.808 ms including routing; the 4.183 ms dense component is the stronger practical comparator.
h200_geometry_and_first_consumer_path.first_consumer: SGLang LogitsProcessor target-verify hidden_states -> retrieval GEMM/top-k -> exact tied-row scorer -> existing softcap and greedy argmax.
h200_geometry_and_first_consumer_path.mapping: Quantize each BF16 hidden row to INT8, run an M=384 N=262144 K=5376 W8A8 GEMM over the immutable rowwise-scaled tied-weight index, fuse per-row top-k, gather only selected BF16 tied rows, and exact-score those rows before the stock monotone softcap/argmax.
h200_geometry_and_first_consumer_path.tile_prior: A 128x128x64 Hopper tensor-core decomposition gives three M tiles, 2048 N tiles, and 84 K steps; 6144 output tiles are enough to fill 132 SMs. The index is HBM-resident, while scale metadata and a fused top-k working set can fit in L2.
